newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia c.bank may regulate banks in securities mkt.
newsitem.headline: Russia c.bank may regulate banks in securities mkt.

text.p: Russia's central bank wants to take over regulation of commercial bank activities on the securities market from the main market watchdog, deputy central bank chairman Andrei Kozlov said on Tuesday.
Kozlov told a banking conference the central bank was discussing the transfer with the State Committee on the Securities Market, previously known as the Federal Commission on the Securities Market.
"Our talks with the Federal Commission on the Securities Market on taking over the right to regulate banks' activities on the stock market are on their final stage," he said.
The State Committee on the Securities Market is currently the only body in Russia with the right to grant licences to capital market participants and supervise their activities.

Last month, a presidential decree downgraded the regulator to a state committee from a federal commission. The move raised fears among brokers that the committee's independence could be undermined and investment into Russian markets would be hurt.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said last month the committee, whose head Dmitry Vasilyev previously had ministerial rank and reported directly to President Boris Yeltsin, was now subordinated to the finance ministry.

But it is not clear this is the final word on the committee. Official documents confirming the new status have not yet been issued, and Vasilyev has not yet been formally reappointed to head the body.
Kozlov said that two weeks ago, the Committee had adopted a regulation allowing it to shift some of its licencing and supervisory rights to other government bodies.
"Now, we are studying the regulation in order to apply to the State Commission to get a general licence to licence banks as professional capital market participants," Kozlov said.
He said the central bank was drawing up plans on regulating banks in the financial markets for when it gets the licence.
It will licence banks as participants on the capital markets, monitor their activities and draw up rules for their conduct and their activities with clients.
Kozlov and Vasilyev clashed last year over the regulation of the government securities market. -- Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow newsroom (095) 941 8520
